intended_object: This is the negation of `HasExponentialBound v` (which says ∃ c>0, ∃ C>0, ∀ n, v n ≤ C·e^{-cn}), with the negation pushed through the quantifiers. It is a helper for a proof by contradiction. I inferred this from the lemma `not_hasExponentialBound_iff` right below it and from its uses in Part04, Part06 and Part09. The docstring is a generic auto-generated one.
explanation: The body is ∀ c>0, ∀ C>0, ∃ n, C·e^{-cn} < v n. This is exactly the pushed-through negation of `HasExponentialBound`, and `not_hasExponentialBound_iff` proves the equivalence with a single `simp only`. Its only job is to support the proof of quantum parallel repetition in Part09. That proof assumes there is no exponential bound, rewrites this as `HasSubexponentialWitness` (repeatedEntangledValue G), and passes that to the later lemmas, which pull out arbitrarily large n where the repeated value exceeds e^{-cn}. So the definition is a proof device with a "witness" name, not a standard notion from the literature. Its mathematical content is just "v is not O(e^{-cn}) for any c>0". The negation is stated correctly. One requirement is that v n > C·e^{-cn} must hold for every C. Since C can be made large enough to beat any finite set of indices, this forces such n to exist arbitrarily far out. That matches the library's follow-up lemma `arbitrarily_large_witness_of_not_hasExponentialBound`.
